candidates.label: H1
candidates.title: ICE's $1 reimbursement allowance behaviorally anchored GEO detainee pay
candidates.description: The nominal reimbursement amount influenced GEO to set pay at or near $1 even though the contract did not impose a legal ceiling.
candidates.falsification: Across comparable facilities, reimbursement changes do not predict pay; GEO/non-GEO operators routinely pay different amounts under the same allowance; internal decision records do not use the ICE rate as the pay reference.

candidates.label: H0
candidates.title: The $1 line was a common administrative allowance and GEO's pay decisions were independently discretionary
candidates.description: Common ICE policy/template language explains the repeated allowance; GEO retained discretion and chose pay based on contractor economics, policy, and local law.
candidates.falsification: Internal GEO/ICE records explicitly use the reimbursement amount as the compensation reference; pay moves with reimbursement within facilities; independent operators converge on $1 only when the allowance is present and diverge when it changes.

evidence_assessments.evidence: Karnes, Broward, and Tacoma repeat a nominal $1 work-program line
evidence_assessments.reason: Both anchoring and common-template explanations predict repeated schedule language.

evidence_assessments.evidence: Tacoma clauses say actual cost of $1 per detainee-day and require CO approval above the displayed amount
evidence_assessments.reason: The language allocates reimbursement/contract authority but does not reveal why GEO chose its pay rate.

evidence_assessments.evidence: Menocal held ICE neither required nor capped GEO pay at $1
evidence_assessments.reason: This defeats a legal-ceiling or mechanical-control theory; a softer behavioral anchor remains possible but unobserved.

evidence_assessments.evidence: Novoa held ICE did not restrict higher pay and GEO controlled wages
evidence_assessments.reason: Independent court/facility confirms discretion but does not observe the contractor's internal reference point.

evidence_assessments.evidence: Another GEO facility reportedly paid as much as $4 while ICE reimbursed at $1
refs: Menocal doc 380 background via 2026-07-13 lead-59489 report
evidence_assessments.reason: Within-firm deviation weighs against mechanical determinism; unidentified facility and lack of full ledger limit weight.

evidence_assessments.evidence: Menocal found GEO's standardized $1 agreement unenforceable
evidence_assessments.reason: Observed $1 choice is explained by either candidate and does not identify causation.

evidence_assessments.evidence: Tacoma final liability and reported profits
evidence_assessments.reason: Large private economics supply an independent cost-minimization incentive; holdings do not decide anchoring.

evidence_assessments.evidence: Common ICE/PBNDS/template ancestry and repeated option-year wording
evidence_assessments.reason: The recurrence count is not independent; a common administrative parent explains it without behavioral influence.

evidence_assessments.evidence: No reimbursement-change/pay-change time series or peer-operator comparison is in the assigned record
evidence_assessments.reason: Missing evidence is a research gap, not affirmative evidence for either candidate.

summary.caveat: Least inconsistent is not confirmation. H1 remains logically possible as an unobserved behavioral effect.
summary.registration_decision: Do not register. The evidence has only two direct, independent no-cap/control adjudications and no third causal context; schedule repetition is dependency-confounded.
